title: Heated domes had higher vapor pressure deficit and more joint high-ozone hours in North Wales in August-September 2021
abstract: We audited drying demand in an ozone and warming experiment with five wildflower species. The complete August-September 2021 record has 1,464 hours. Heated domes had 0.71-0.90 kPa higher mean air vapor pressure deficit than a shared ambient reference. Hours with deficit at least 2 kPa and ozone at least 60 ppb were more common by 12.50 and 6.90 percentage points at the 80 and 110 ppb targets. The 30 ppb target had no such hours. An exact vapor-pressure identity separates saturation pressure from actual water vapor. June-July had only 24.59 percent weather coverage. Sharp missing-hour bounds permit either sign of its joint-exposure differences. Sparse flower visits show fewer species in flower in heated domes, but one dome per treatment, one site, one year and shared ambient weather prevent a causal plant-response claim or geographic replication. We provide original code, source hashes, aggregate results and a figure. Source records stay external.

display.caption: Same-hour mean VPD differences, joint high-VPD and high-ozone hour shares, and sharp missing-hour bounds. Seasonal windows share domes and an ambient weather reference. Bounds do not include sensor error.
